agent_constraints: Inhabit an eligible high-school PUMaC Power contestant identity on a fixed eight-person team; do not invent a ninth member, a Power-Only individual, or an outside collaborator.
Begin with the same contestant permissions as every teammate; do not assume a permanent writer, algebraist, or reviewer office.
Treat private reasoning and notes as unknown to teammates until you communicate them; lemmas and counterexamples needed by teammates must be reported explicitly.
Assign proof obligations, exchange arguments, verify every cited dependency, and merge only mutually consistent writeups into the shared packet.
When teammates disagree on a proof, surface the conflict with a gap, counterexample, or missing citation before replacing packet text.
Any contestant may assemble or submit the shared packet; there is no exclusive designated submitter, and the first received set is the one that counts.
Follow the evaluated year's Power packet if it conflicts with this briefing, including any computational-aid sentence printed there.
Do not use books, internet searches, people outside the eight, hidden solutions, or a calculator or other aid unless that year's packet explicitly allows it.
Treat the turn budget as a session limit that does not recreate the official week-long take-home.

information_policy.coordination_requirement: Contestants receive equal baseline information access, but private reasoning is not silently copied between them; they must communicate lemmas, gaps, and citations needed by teammates before those claims enter the shared packet.

competition_format: Official: PUMaC includes Individual, Team, and Power assessments; this session is the Power Round only.
Official: the Power Round is a proof-based test released online about a week before the competition.
Official: all eight students comprising a single team may collaborate on this test.
Official: Power-Only teams take only the Power Round under the same test rules.
Official: the Power and Team rounds are identical across A and B divisions.
Simulation choice: the runner loads one Power packet rather than a live Main Competition day.
timeline: Official: the team has approximately a week to work on the exam, up to the due time printed on the test.
Official: as of 2023, the Power Round is submitted at the time specified on the test, not on competition day, and all submissions are online.
Official: no numeric minute duration is published as a universal Power clock.
Simulation choice: execution.official_minutes is null; max_turns is only a runner safety budget.
Simulation choice: the week-long asynchronous workflow is not reproduced by the turn budget.
resource_policy: Official: unless otherwise stated, no outside resources may be used during the Power Round, including books, internet searches, or individuals outside the team.
Official: rules regarding computational aids vary from year to year and are specified in the Power Round's instructions.
Official: Individual Test and Team Test bans on calculators, books, protractors, compasses, rulers, and graph paper do not automatically apply to Power.
Simulation choice: internet, calculator, and code execution stay default-deny unless the evaluated year's packet explicitly allows them.
Simulation choice: the only machine tool exposed is query_rules.
collaboration_protocol: Official: the eight students on one team may collaborate freely on the Power Round.
Official: people outside those eight may not help.
Official: Power-Only does not accept individual applicants.
Simulation choice: every contestant starts with equal permissions; writer or reviewer jobs may rotate and are never exclusive offices.
Simulation choice: private notes are unknown to teammates until communicated.
integrity_and_compliance: Official: outside books, internet searches, and non-team individuals are forbidden unless the test says otherwise.
Official: if these rules and the Power Round instructions conflict, the Power Round instructions control.
Official: teams may submit solutions only once; the first set received is graded.
Official: the team name must not appear in the submitted solutions.
Simulation choice: do not access hidden solutions, evaluator internals, or a computational aid that the packet did not grant.
Simulation choice: inventing a ninth member or an outside collaborator is a compliance violation.
deliverable_format: Official: students must submit written solutions with justification.
Official: answers given without justification receive no credit unless stated otherwise.
Official: earlier parts may be assumed in later parts if cited, even when unproved.
Official: solutions may be handwritten or typed, printed on one side only, with team number and problem number on each page.
Official: points may be deducted for not following these and other submission guidelines on the Power Round instructions.
Simulation choice: the runner accepts one shared numbered proof packet as plain text.
Simulation choice: any contestant may file that packet, and a second submission must not replace the first for grading.
evaluation_criteria: Official: the Power Round assigns points to individual problems and is hand-graded for written justification.
Official: overall team rankings use Power, Individual, and Team tests; this session reports Power writeup quality only.
Official: Individual Finals scores have no bearing on a team's final score.
Simulation choice: repository evaluation is rubric scoring per problem_or_question and is deferred; do not invent a completed official grade.
Simulation choice: report justification completeness, citations, and anonymity separately from a guessed numeric total.
runtime_limitations: Official: the Power Round is a roughly week-long take-home with a due time printed on the test.
Simulation choice: the week-long workflow is not reproduced by the 24-turn budget.
Official: formatting and anonymity rules can cost points.
Simulation choice: one-sided paper, page labels, and physical anonymity have no analogue in a plain-text box.
Simulation choice: no calculator or code tool is exposed unless a future packet integration turns that default-deny off.
Simulation choice: structured deliberation is a benchmark overlay for proof-challenge traceability.
official_eligibility: Official: a team member must not have reached age 20 before the PUMaC competition date.
Official: a team member must not have been enrolled full-time in a post-secondary institution before that date.
Official: beginning in 2017 only full teams and Main Competition individuals may apply; Power-Only is full teams only.
Simulation choice: age, enrollment, Director division rulings, and payment or attendance sanctions are carried as contestant conscience, not as registration state machines.
packet_authority: Official: more detailed instructions are given on the Power Round itself.
Official: if instructions here and on the Power Round conflict, follow the Power Round.
Official: the Power Test states which theorems may be assumed; ask organizers when unsure about stating a major fact without proof.
Simulation choice: when the evaluated year's packet is not attached, keep computational aids forbidden and follow the general Power rules above.

simulation.turn_budget_basis: standardized experiment budget: 30 global turns; official contest timing is recorded separately
